name: United Nations
trivia: Adopted in 1946; features a polar azimuthal equidistant projection map surrounded by olive branches symbolizing global peace.

name: European Union
trivia: Features a circle of 12 golden stars on an azure blue field, representing ideals of unity, solidarity, and harmony across European peoples.

name: NATO
trivia: Adopted in 1953; the navy field represents the Atlantic Ocean, and the compass rose points the collective path toward common peace.

name: African Union
trivia: Adopted in 2010; features 55 golden stars on a dark green field surrounding a green map silhouette of the African continent.

name: ASEAN
trivia: Depicts ten yellow rice stalks bound together in a red circle on blue, symbolizing solidarity and friendship across Southeast Asia.

name: Arab League
trivia: Adopted in 1945; features a green field with a white crescent and a 22-link chain symbolizing solidarity between Arab nations.

name: Olympic Movement
trivia: Designed in 1913 by Pierre de Coubertin; the five interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green, red) represent the inhabited continents of the globe.

name: International Red Cross
officialName: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
trivia: Formed in 1863 as the exact colour inversion of the flag of Switzerland, honoring founder Henry Dunant's Swiss homeland.

name: Commonwealth of Nations
trivia: Features a golden globe radiating spears that form the letter 'C' for Commonwealth, set against a deep ocean-blue field.

name: Nordic Council
trivia: Depicts a stylized white swan with eight wing feathers flying across a blue disc, symbolizing cooperation between the Nordic countries and regions.

name: OPEC
officialName: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
trivia: Features a stylized circular monogram of the letters O-P-E-C on a light blue petroleum field, adopted in 1970.

name: CARICOM
trivia: Consists of light blue (sky) and dark blue (sea) stripes, with a golden yellow sun and overlapping green 'C's for Caribbean Community.

name: CEFTA
trivia: Established in 1992 in Visegrád, Hungary, to facilitate economic cooperation and trade integration across Southeastern Europe.

name: East African Community
trivia: Founded in 1967 and revitalised in 2000; represents 8 partner states in the African Great Lakes region headquartered in Arusha, Tanzania.

name: Soviet Union (USSR)
trivia: Iconic red banner with golden hammer (industrial workers), sickle (peasants), and red star, representing the superpower from 1922 until its 1991 dissolution.

name: East Germany (DDR)
trivia: Defaced the traditional black-red-gold tricolor with the socialist emblem: a compass (intellectuals) and hammer (workers) inside a wreath of rye.

name: Yugoslavia (SFRY)
trivia: Pan-Slavic blue-white-red tricolor charged with a red socialist star edged in gold, flown during Marshal Josip Broz Tito's federation.

name: Ottoman Empire
trivia: Adopted in 1844 by Sultan Abdulmejid I; the red banner with a white crescent and star directly inspired the modern Turkish national flag.

name: Kingdom of Prussia
trivia: Black and white horizontal stripes featuring the crowned Prussian Black Eagle grasping a scepter and orb, originating from the Teutonic Order.

name: Austria-Hungary
trivia: The dual monarchy's 1869 civil ensign split the bottom stripe: red-white-red with Austrian crest on the hoist, red-white-green with Crown of St. Stephen on the fly.

name: Russian Empire
trivia: The 1858 black-yellow-white tricolor was the first official state flag of the Russian Empire, representing monasticism, imperial glory, and purity.

name: Qing Dynasty
trivia: Adopted in 1889 as China's first national flag; features the imperial Azure Dragon chasing a red flaming pearl on a golden yellow field.

name: Republic of Texas
trivia: Adopted in 1839 as the national flag of the sovereign Republic of Texas, featuring a single white star on blue with red and white stripes.

name: South Vietnam
trivia: A golden yellow field with three horizontal red stripes representing Northern, Central, and Southern Vietnam, originating from Emperor Thanh Thai in 1890.

name: Byzantine Empire
trivia: The Palaiologos dynasty imperial flag featured a red cross on red with four golden firesteels (B letters) representing 'King of Kings, Ruling over Kings'.

name: Roman Empire (SPQR)
trivia: The legendary Roman imperial vexillum: an eagle surrounded by a laurel wreath and 'SPQR' (The Senate and People of Rome) in imperial gold upon crimson red.

name: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
officialName: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (TTPI)
trivia: A UN trust territory in Micronesia administered by the US from 1947 to 1994; its 6 white stars represented the Mariana, Marshall, Palau, Ponape, Truk, and Yap districts.

name: Holy Roman Empire
trivia: The Reichsadler (imperial double-headed eagle with halos) on a gold banner symbolized supreme secular authority over Christian realms.

name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
officialName: Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania
trivia: Known as the Commonwealth of the Two Nations; the royal banner combined the White Eagle of Poland with the armed Vytis knight of Lithuania.

name: Kingdom of Hawaii
trivia: Commissioned by King Kamehameha I; its 8 alternating white, red, and blue stripes represent the major Hawaiian islands alongside a British Union Jack canton.

name: California Republic
trivia: Crafted in 1846 by American settlers in Sonoma led by William B. Ide; featured a grizzly bear and red star on cotton, inspiring the modern state flag.

name: Mughal Empire
trivia: The Alam banner was triangular moss green with a golden lion passant looking back at a radiant golden sun rising over its back.

name: Gran Colombia
trivia: Founded by Simón Bolívar, uniting Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama; its yellow, blue, and red tricolor inspired all three successor national flags.

name: Republic of Genoa
trivia: A dominant maritime power across the Mediterranean for eight centuries; its red St. George's cross on white was licensed to English ships in 1190 for protection.

name: First French Empire
trivia: The personal standard of Napoléon I featured the Imperial eagle grasping Jupiter's thunderbolt with golden bees symbolizing French immortality.

name: Safavid Empire
trivia: Adopted by Shah Ismail II; features a golden lion and rising sun (Shir-o-Khorshid) on a green field, establishing Iran's classical national emblem.

name: Republic of Ragusa
trivia: A prosperous seafaring republic on the Dalmatian coast; the flag depicts patron saint St. Blaise (Sveti Vlaho) holding a model of the walled city.

name: Kingdom of Scotland (Royal Standard)
officialName: Royal Banner of the Royal Arms of Scotland
trivia: The famed 'Lion Rampant' banner; features a red lion with blue tongue and claws rearing within a double royal tressure on golden yellow.

name: Kingdom of Ireland (Green Harp)
trivia: First flown by Owen Roe O'Neill in 1642; the golden Celtic harp on St. Patrick's emerald green field became Ireland's universal freedom symbol.

name: Grand Duchy of Finland
trivia: An autonomous grand duchy that paved the way to Finnish independence; features the red and gold Finnish lion rampant trampling a Russian sabre.

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
trivia: Ruled Japan during the peaceful Edo period; the naval ensign features a bold black horizontal bar on a clean white field.

name: Korean Empire
trivia: Proclaimed by Emperor Gojong in 1897; features an early dynamic red and blue Taegeuk circle with four trigrams, precursor to the South Korean flag.

name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
trivia: Known as the Derafsh-e Shahbaz (Standard of Cyrus the Great); displays a golden royal falcon or eagle with spread wings holding two solar discs on garnet red.

name: Chicago
trivia: Ranked #2 all-time in American city flag design by the NAVA: two sky-blue stripes (Lake Michigan and river) and four 6-pointed red stars for major historical milestones.

name: Washington, D.C.
trivia: Ranked #1 best American city flag design: based directly on George Washington's family coat of arms with two red bars and three red stars on white.

name: Amsterdam
trivia: World-famous for minimalist power: a bold red field with a black central band charged with three white St. Andrew's Crosses (saltires).

name: City of London
trivia: Features the red St. George's Cross on white, with the red upright sword of Saint Paul (London's patron saint) in the upper hoist canton.

name: Paris
trivia: Vertical blue and red bicolor featuring the city coat of arms with an ancient silver galley ship over waves, bearing motto 'Fluctuat nec mergitur'.

name: Tokyo
trivia: Adopted in 1943; features a white six-rayed stylized sun emblem on an Edo-purple field, symbolizing Tokyo as Japan's radiant capital.

name: Venice
trivia: One of the most complex flags on Earth: deep red field with gold scrollwork, featuring the winged Lion of Saint Mark with six split fringed tails representing the sestieri.

name: Berlin
trivia: White field bordered by red stripes, displaying the iconic Berlin Bear ('Berliner Bär') standing rampant with red tongue and claws.

name: Madrid
trivia: Crimson field with the city's historic coat of arms: a black bear reaching up into a strawberry tree (Madroño), surrounded by seven white stars.

name: Rome
trivia: Vertical bicolor of imperial dark red (purple) and golden yellow, honoring the historic imperial colors of the ancient Roman Republic and Empire.

name: Los Angeles
trivia: The 'Fiesta Flag': notched tricolor of green (olive trees), gold (orange groves), and red (vineyards) with the city seal at its center.

name: Toronto
trivia: Designed by 21-year-old student Renato De Santis; white geometric towers of City Hall form the letter 'T' with a red maple leaf at its base.

name: Rio de Janeiro
trivia: White field with a blue saltire of St. Sebastian (patron saint), charged with the city arms featuring the Phrygian cap and dolphin supporters.

name: Buenos Aires
trivia: White field charged with the Habsburg black eagle holding the red Cross of Calatrava in its claws, granted by founder Juan de Garay in 1580.

name: Montreal
trivia: St. George's Cross on white with 5 symbols: French fleur-de-lys, English rose, Scottish thistle, Irish shamrock, and an indigenous White Pine at the center.

name: Barcelona
trivia: Quartered flag combining the red St. George's cross on white with the Catalan Senyera (four vertical red bars on golden yellow).

name: New York City
trivia: The blue, white, and orange vertical tricolor commemorates the 17th-century Dutch Republic flag of New Amsterdam, with the municipal seal in the center.

name: San Francisco
officialName: City and County of San Francisco
trivia: Features a golden phoenix rising from ashes above the Spanish motto 'Oro en Paz, Fierro en Guerra' (Gold in Peace, Iron in War), bordered in gold.

name: St. Louis
trivia: Ranked the #5 best city flag in America by NAVA; wavy blue and white stripes represent the confluence of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers.

name: Denver
trivia: Designed by high school student Margaret Overbeck in 1926; red zig-zag represents the Rocky Mountains under a yellow sun and deep blue sky.

name: New Orleans
trivia: Adopted in 1918 for the city's bicentennial; features a large white center stripe with three golden fleurs-de-lis representing French heritage.

name: Brussels
trivia: Features a stylized yellow iris with grey border centered on a blue field, symbolizing the yellow marsh irises that once grew around early Brussels.

name: Vienna
trivia: Consists of two equal horizontal bands of red and white, matching the colors of the Austrian Babenberg dynasty coat of arms.

name: Seoul
trivia: Features a green wave, blue mountain peak, and red solar disc representing Seoul's harmony between the Han River, Mt. Namsan, and vibrant citizens.

name: Kyoto
trivia: Adopted in 1960; features a stylized lattice crest based on the kanji '京' (kyo) in radiant gold on a deep purple field, the traditional imperial color.
